title: Postpartum haemorrhage: 4 Ts, uterotonic ladder & surgical steps
subject: OBGY
anchor: Boggy, uterus above umbilicus + heavy bleeding after delivery = atonic PPH (Tone, ~70%)
Well-contracted uterus but still bleeding → Trauma (tears, haematoma, rupture, inversion)
Shock out of proportion to visible loss → concealed bleed (broad-ligament/vulval haematoma, inversion, rupture); shock index ≥0.9–1.0 = alarm
Ladder: oxytocin → ergometrine → carboprost / misoprostol + TXA → balloon tamponade → B-Lynch / devascularisation → hysterectomy
algorithm:
Call for help, 2 large-bore IV, crossmatch, O₂, warm crystalloid, catheterise (monitor UO)
→ Bimanual uterine compression + uterine massage; check placenta complete, inspect genital tract
→ Oxytocin 10 IU IM/slow IV + 20–40 IU in 1 L infusion
→ Ergometrine/methylergometrine 0.2 mg IM/slow IV (NOT in HTN/pre-eclampsia/heart disease)
→ Carboprost (15-methyl PGF₂α) 250 µg IM q15 min, max 8 doses = 2 mg (NOT in asthma)
  or misoprostol 800 µg sublingual
→ Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 min within 3 h of birth; 2nd 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 min
→ Still bleeding: intrauterine balloon tamponade (Bakri / condom catheter)
  → if fails: laparotomy → B-Lynch compression suture
  → stepwise devascularisation: uterine artery (O'Leary) → ovarian → internal iliac (anterior division) ligation
  → hysterectomy (life-saving, do not delay); IR embolisation if stable & available
Retained tissue → manual removal/evacuation; inversion → immediate manual replacement (Johnson), then O'Sullivan hydrostatic / Huntington / Haultain
Coagulopathy (Thrombin) → blood products (massive transfusion ratio), fibrinogen

0.2 mg IM or slow IV; repeat q2–4 h (max 1 mg)

Contraindicated in bronchial asthma (bronchospasm); diarrhoea, fever
Heat-stable, cheap; shivering, pyrexia; useful in community settings

points: **Definition**: WHO ≥500 mL within 24 h of birth (severe ≥1000 mL); ACOG 2017 reVITALize: cumulative ≥1000 mL or loss with signs of hypovolaemia within 24 h, any route. Exam-classic: ≥500 mL vaginal, ≥1000 mL caesarean
**Primary** PPH within 24 h; **secondary** 24 h to 12 weeks (commonest causes: retained products, endometritis)
**4 Ts**: Tone (~70%) > Trauma (~20%) > Tissue (~10%) > Thrombin (<1%); atony is the commonest cause
**AMTSL** (prevention): uterotonic (oxytocin 10 IU IM) immediately after birth + controlled cord traction + delayed cord clamping (1–3 min); oxytocin is the uterotonic of choice
Haemorrhage (mainly PPH) is the leading direct cause of maternal death in India

**Internal iliac ligation**: tie the anterior division (distal to the posterior division to spare gluteal supply); it ↓ pulse pressure distal to ligation (~85%) rather than abolishing flow, so fertility is preserved
**B-Lynch**: brace suture compressing the uterus; test efficacy first by bimanual compression at laparotomy
Non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG) is a first-aid bridge during referral
Placenta accreta spectrum is a leading indication for emergency peripartum hysterectomy

traps.stem: Severe pre-eclampsia, atonic PPH not responding to oxytocin. Next uterotonic?
traps.trap: Methylergometrine – it is the classic 2nd drug in the ladder
traps.fix: Ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertension/pre-eclampsia (risk of hypertensive crisis, stroke) → use carboprost (if no asthma) or misoprostol

traps.stem: Asthmatic woman with atonic PPH after oxytocin fails
traps.fix: PGF₂α causes bronchospasm → avoid; use ergometrine (if normotensive) or misoprostol (PGE₁)

traps.stem: PPH, uterus firm and well contracted, placenta complete, bleeding continues
traps.fix: Contracted uterus with bleeding = trauma (cervical/vaginal tear) → examine under anaesthesia and repair

cards.back: 250 µg IM every 15–90 min, max 8 doses (2 mg); contraindicated in bronchial asthma

cards.back: Uterine atony (Tone ~70% of the 4 Ts)

title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, eclampsia & MgSO₄
subject: OBGY
anchor: New BP ≥140/90 after 20 wk + proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction = pre-eclampsia
Seizure in pre-eclampsia with no other cause = eclampsia → MgSO₄ (drug of choice), then deliver after stabilisation
Haemolysis + ↑ AST/ALT + platelets <100,000 = HELLP (can occur with normal BP)
MgSO₄ toxicity order: loss of patellar reflex → respiratory depression → cardiac arrest; antidote calcium gluconate 1 g IV
algorithm:
BP ≥140/90 on 2 readings ≥4 h apart after 20 wk
→ No proteinuria, no severe features → gestational hypertension
→ Proteinuria (≥300 mg/24 h or PCR ≥0.3 or dipstick ≥2+) OR new end-organ dysfunction → pre-eclampsia
  → Severe features? SBP ≥160 / DBP ≥110, platelets <100,000, LFT >2× ULN or RUQ pain, creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubled, pulmonary oedema, new headache / visual symptoms
    → Yes: MgSO₄ + IV labetalol / oral nifedipine / IV hydralazine (target <160/110); steroids if <34 wk; deliver at ≥34 wk (earlier if unstable)
    → No: monitor, deliver at 37 wk
→ Seizure → eclampsia: ABC, left lateral, MgSO₄ loading, control BP, deliver once stable (mode by obstetric indication)
Before every MgSO₄ maintenance dose: patellar reflex present + RR ≥16/min + urine ≥30 mL/h (≥100 mL in 4 h)
→ Any absent → withhold dose; respiratory depression → calcium gluconate 10% 10 mL (1 g) IV over 10 min

tables.title: MgSO₄ regimens
head: Regimen
Loading
Maintenance
rows: 4 g of 20% IV over 5–15 min + 10 g of 50% deep IM (5 g each buttock) = 14 g
5 g of 50% deep IM every 4 h in alternate buttocks
Continue 24 h after delivery or after last seizure, whichever later
Therapeutic level 4–7 mEq/L; reflexes lost ~10; respiratory paralysis ~12–15; cardiac arrest >25 mEq/L

tables.title: Spectrum
head: Entity
Defining feature
rows: HTN before pregnancy or before 20 wk (or persisting >12 wk postpartum)
New HTN ≥20 wk, no proteinuria, no end-organ involvement
New HTN ≥20 wk + proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction (proteinuria no longer mandatory)
Chronic HTN + new proteinuria / end-organ dysfunction
Pre-eclampsia + generalised tonic-clonic seizures (antepartum commonest; postpartum up to 6 wk)
Haemolysis (LDH ≥600 IU/L, schistocytes), AST/ALT >2× ULN (≥70 IU/L), platelets <100,000

points: Pathogenesis: failed 2nd-wave trophoblast invasion of spiral arteries → placental ischaemia → ↑ sFlt-1, ↓ PlGF → endothelial dysfunction; renal hallmark = **glomerular endotheliosis**
ACOG 2019/2020: massive proteinuria (>5 g) and fetal growth restriction are **no longer** severe features
Acute severe HTN drugs: **labetalol** IV 20 → 40 → 80 mg q10 min; **nifedipine** IR oral 10–20 mg; **hydralazine** 5–10 mg IV. Avoid ACE-I/ARBs (fetal renal dysgenesis) and atenolol (FGR)
Long-term antihypertensives in pregnancy: labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa

**Aspirin** prophylaxis 75–150 mg at night, start 12–16 wk (before 16 wk best) until 36 wk, in high-risk women (prior pre-eclampsia, chronic HTN, DM, renal disease, SLE/APS, multifetal) – ASPRE used 150 mg
Calcium 1.5–2 g/day reduces pre-eclampsia in populations with low dietary calcium (WHO)
Delivery is the only cure; eclampsia/HELLP → deliver after maternal stabilisation regardless of gestation
MgSO₄ is also given for fetal neuroprotection when delivery <32 wk anticipated
Commonest causes of maternal death in pre-eclampsia: intracranial haemorrhage and pulmonary oedema

traps.stem: On Pritchard regimen: knee jerk present, RR 18/min, urine 60 mL in last 4 h. Next 5 g IM dose due
traps.trap: Give the dose – reflexes and breathing are fine
traps.fix: Withhold: urine output must be ≥100 mL/4 h (≥30 mL/h) because Mg is renally excreted; review fluids, check Mg level

traps.stem: Eclamptic fit controlled with MgSO₄, BP 170/112
traps.trap: Immediate caesarean before BP is controlled
traps.fix: Stabilise first: control BP (<160/110) and fits, then deliver; mode by obstetric indication (vaginal not contraindicated)

traps.stem: Which drug controls eclamptic seizures best and prevents recurrence?
traps.fix: MgSO₄ (Collaborative Eclampsia Trial 1995) – superior to both

cards.back: Patellar reflex present, RR ≥16/min, urine output ≥30 mL/h (≥100 mL in 4 h)

cards.front: Antidote to MgSO₄ toxicity and dose?
cards.back: Calcium gluconate 10%, 10 mL (1 g) IV slowly over ~10 min

cards.back: Haemolysis (LDH ≥600, schistocytes), AST/ALT ≥70 IU/L (>2× ULN), platelets <100,000/µL

title: Antepartum haemorrhage: previa vs abruption vs vasa previa, PAS
subject: OBGY
anchor: Painless, causeless, recurrent bright-red bleeding + soft non-tender uterus + high head/malpresentation = placenta previa
Painful dark bleeding + tense, tender 'woody-hard' uterus + fetal distress/death ± DIC = abruption
Bleeding at rupture of membranes + sudden fetal bradycardia/sinusoidal pattern with a stable mother = vasa previa (fetal blood – Apt test)
Previa + previous caesarean = placenta accreta spectrum until proven otherwise
algorithm:
APH (bleeding after 20 wk; Indian texts: 28 wk) → resuscitate, crossmatch, anti-D if Rh-negative
→ NO per-vaginal / per-speculum digital exam until previa excluded (USG first; TVS is safe & most accurate)
→ Previa on USG:
  → Heavy bleeding / labour / fetal distress / ≥37 wk → caesarean
  → Preterm, stable → expectant (Macafee–Johnson): admit, steroids 24–34 wk, blood ready; planned CS 36⁺⁰–37⁺⁶ wk
→ Abruption (clinical diagnosis; USG misses most):
  → Fetus alive + distress → urgent CS
  → Fetus dead → ARM + oxytocin, vaginal delivery preferred; correct DIC
→ Vasa previa diagnosed antenatally (TVS colour Doppler) → admit ~30–32 wk, steroids, planned CS 34–37 wk; bleeding at ROM → emergency CS

tables.title: APH: three-way contrast
head: Feature
Placenta previa
Abruptio placentae
Vasa previa
rows: Rapid bradycardia, sinusoidal; high fetal mortality
Previous CS, multiparity, age, smoking, multiple pregnancy
Hypertension (commonest), trauma, cocaine, smoking, sudden decompression
Velamentous cord, bilobed/succenturiate placenta, IVF, low placenta
DIC, Couvelaire uterus, AKI, PPH, Sheehan

points: **Classification (current)**: placenta previa = covers internal os; low-lying = edge within 20 mm of os. Old Types I–IV (IV = central/complete; II posterior is 'dangerous' – compresses cord against sacral promontory)
**Apt test**: alkali denaturation – fetal HbF resists NaOH and stays pink; adult Hb turns yellow-brown
**Couvelaire uterus** (uteroplacental apoplexy): blood extravasates into myometrium in concealed abruption; uterus usually still contracts – it is NOT an indication for hysterectomy by itself
Abruption is the commonest cause of DIC in pregnancy (consumption → low fibrinogen)
**Placenta accreta spectrum** (absent decidua basalis/Nitabuch layer): accreta = villi on myometrium; increta = into myometrium; percreta = through serosa ± bladder
PAS USG/MRI signs: loss of retroplacental clear zone, placental lacunae ('Swiss cheese'), bladder wall interruption, hypervascularity
PAS management: planned caesarean hysterectomy at 34⁺⁰–35⁺⁶ wk, placenta left in situ (do not attempt removal), fundal/classical incision
Stallworthy sign: FHR slows when the head is pressed into the pelvis in posterior previa
Double set-up examination (in OT) only if USG unavailable and delivery being planned

traps.stem: G3P2 with previous CS, 32 wk, painless bright red bleeding, soft uterus. Registrar wants a PV to assess the cervix
traps.fix: Never do PV in suspected previa – can provoke torrential bleed; confirm with USG (TVS is safe)

traps.stem: Bleeding begins at amniotomy, fetal heart drops to 70/min, mother haemodynamically stable
traps.fix: Vasa previa – fetal vessel rupture; immediate caesarean; Apt test shows fetal blood

traps.stem: Concealed abruption, uterus bluish and ecchymotic at CS but contracts with oxytocin
traps.fix: Conserve the uterus; hysterectomy only for uncontrollable PPH

cards.front: Test to differentiate fetal from maternal blood in vaginal bleeding?
cards.back: Apt test (alkali denaturation): fetal HbF stays pink; adult Hb turns brown. Also Kleihauer–Betke

cards.text: Most common risk factor for abruption is {{c1::maternal hypertension}}; most important risk for PAS is {{c2::placenta previa with previous caesarean}}.

cards.front: Why no PV exam in APH before USG?
cards.back: May dislodge a previa and cause massive haemorrhage

cards.text: In placenta {{c1::percreta}} villi penetrate the serosa and may invade the {{c2::bladder}}.

cards.front: Couvelaire uterus – definition and implication?
cards.back: Extravasation of blood into myometrium in abruption; not by itself an indication for hysterectomy

Placenta accreta spectrum: accreta (to myometrium) → increta (into myometrium) → percreta (through serosa)

title: Cervical screening, CIN & FIGO 2018 cervical cancer
subject: OBGY
anchor: Postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding in a multiparous woman with friable cervical growth = carcinoma cervix (HPV 16/18)
Screen-and-treat: VIA positive (acetowhite area) → cryo/thermal ablation in same visit
Parametrium involved (IIB) or tumour >4 cm (IB3/IIA2) → concurrent chemoradiation, NOT radical hysterectomy
Commonest cause of death in Ca cervix: uraemia from bilateral ureteric obstruction
algorithm:
Screening → abnormal
→ ASC-US → reflex HPV DNA: + → colposcopy; – → routine (or repeat cytology at 1 yr)
→ LSIL → colposcopy (≥25 y)
→ ASC-H / HSIL → colposcopy ± directed biopsy (HSIL: 'see-and-treat' LEEP acceptable)
→ AGC → colposcopy + endocervical sampling (+ endometrial sampling if ≥35 y or risk)
Biopsy → CIN 1 → observe (most regress); CIN 2/3 → excision (LEEP/LLETZ, cold-knife cone) or ablation if eligible
→ Invasive → FIGO stage:
  IA1 (no LVSI) → extrafascial hysterectomy / cone if fertility desired
  IA1 + LVSI, IA2 → modified radical hysterectomy + pelvic LND (or radical trachelectomy)
  IB1, IB2, IIA1 → radical (Wertheim) hysterectomy + pelvic LND, or primary CCRT
  IB3, IIA2 → CCRT preferred
  IIB–IVA → CCRT (EBRT + brachytherapy + weekly cisplatin)
  IVB → systemic chemotherapy ± palliative RT

head: Stage
Definition
rows: Microscopic; stromal invasion <3 mm / 3 to <5 mm (horizontal spread no longer counted)
Invasion ≥5 mm; tumour ≤2 cm / >2–≤4 cm / >4 cm
Upper 2/3 vagina, no parametrium; ≤4 cm / >4 cm
Parametrium involved, not up to pelvic wall
Lower 1/3 vagina / pelvic side wall and/or hydronephrosis or non-functioning kidney
Pelvic / para-aortic lymph nodes (r = imaging, p = pathology)
Bladder or rectal mucosa (biopsy-proven; bullous oedema not enough) / distant metastasis

tables.title: Screening tests & intervals
head: Programme
Test & interval
rows: VIA by trained health worker, women 30–65 y, every 5 y; screen-and-treat
HPV DNA primary test from 30 y, every 5–10 y (VIA/cytology if HPV test unavailable)
HPV DNA from 25 y, every 3–5 y
Cytology every 3 y from 21–29; at 30–65: HPV every 5 y, co-test every 5 y, or cytology every 3 y

points: **HPV 16** commonest overall (squamous); **HPV 18** linked to adenocarcinoma; E6 degrades **p53**, E7 inactivates **Rb**
**Bethesda 2014**: NILM, ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL, HSIL, SCC; glandular: AGC, AIS, adenocarcinoma
Transformation zone (squamocolumnar junction) is where CIN arises; colposcopy is inadequate if the SCJ is not fully visible
VIA uses 3–5% acetic acid (acetowhite); VILI uses Lugol's iodine (abnormal areas stay mustard-yellow, iodine-negative = Schiller test)
**HPV vaccines**: bivalent (16,18), quadrivalent (6,11,16,18; Indian Cervavac is qHPV), 9-valent (6,11,16,18,31,33,45,52,58)
Schedule: 9–14 y → 2 doses 0 and 6–12 mo; ≥15 y or immunocompromised → 3 doses (0, 1–2, 6 mo). WHO 2022 also allows a single dose for 9–20 y
LACC trial (2018): minimally invasive radical hysterectomy had worse survival → open approach preferred
Commonest histology squamous cell carcinoma (~80%); commonest site of distant spread: para-aortic nodes, lung
CIN in pregnancy: colposcopy safe, no endocervical curettage; defer treatment until after delivery unless invasion suspected

traps.fix: Parametrial involvement = IIB → concurrent chemoradiation; size is irrelevant once parametrium is involved

traps.trap: Stage stays IB1 because FIGO is clinical

traps.fix: Any hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney attributable to tumour = IIIB

title: Endometrial hyperplasia & cancer; ovarian tumours and markers
subject: OBGY
anchor: Obese, diabetic, nulliparous postmenopausal woman with bleeding = endometrial carcinoma until biopsy says otherwise
Young girl, rapidly enlarging solid ovarian mass, ↑ LDH = dysgerminoma; ↑ AFP = yolk sac tumour (Schiller–Duval bodies)
Postmenopausal bleeding + endometrial thickening + adnexal mass with ↑ inhibin = granulosa cell tumour (Call–Exner bodies)
Bilateral solid ovarian masses with signet-ring cells = Krukenberg (stomach primary)
algorithm:
Postmenopausal bleeding → TVS endometrial thickness
  ≤4 mm → low risk (biopsy if bleeding persists)
  >4 mm → endometrial sampling (Pipelle) ± hysteroscopy-guided biopsy
→ Hyperplasia without atypia → progestogen (LNG-IUS first line) × ≥6 mo; repeat biopsy at 6 mo
→ Atypical hyperplasia / EIN → total hysterectomy ± BSO (no ablation); high-dose progestin/LNG-IUS only if fertility wanted
→ Carcinoma → surgical staging: total hysterectomy + BSO + sentinel/pelvic ± para-aortic nodes + washings
Adnexal mass → USG (IOTA simple rules / O-RADS) + CA-125 → RMI
  RMI >200 or IOTA malignant → gynae-oncology: staging laparotomy, maximal cytoreduction + carboplatin–paclitaxel
  Young + solid mass → AFP, β-hCG, LDH (germ cell) → fertility-sparing USO + BEP

tables.title: Ovarian tumours
head: Group
Examples & markers
Discriminators
rows: Serous (commonest; psammoma bodies), mucinous (largest; CEA/CA 19-9), endometrioid & clear cell (endometriosis-associated), Brenner (Walthard nests, coffee-bean nuclei); CA-125
High-grade serous arises from fallopian-tube fimbria (STIC); BRCA1/2, Lynch
Mature cystic teratoma/dermoid (commonest GCT, benign); dysgerminoma – LDH, PLAP; yolk sac – AFP; choriocarcinoma – β-hCG; embryonal – AFP + hCG; immature teratoma (neuroepithelium)
Dysgerminoma: commonest malignant GCT, bilateral ~10–15%, very radiosensitive; struma ovarii → hyperthyroidism
Granulosa cell – inhibin, AMH (oestrogen: precocious puberty, endometrial hyperplasia; Call–Exner, FOXL2); thecoma; fibroma (Meigs); Sertoli–Leydig – androgens (virilisation)
Fibroma + ascites + (right) pleural effusion = Meigs, resolves after removal
Krukenberg: bilateral, mucin-filled signet-ring cells; stomach > colon, breast

points: **WHO 2014 (retained 2020)** hyperplasia: without atypia (progression ~1–3%) vs atypical hyperplasia/EIN (risk of coexisting or future cancer high, up to ~40%). Old Kurman 1985: simple 1%, complex 3%, simple atypical 8%, complex atypical 29%
**Type I** endometrial Ca: endometrioid, oestrogen-driven, PTEN, younger obese, good prognosis. **Type II**: serous/clear cell, p53, older thin, poor prognosis

**FIGO 2009** endometrium (exam-classic): IA <50% myometrium, IB ≥50%, II cervical stroma, IIIA serosa/adnexa, IIIB vagina/parametrium, IIIC1 pelvic / IIIC2 para-aortic nodes, IVA bladder/bowel mucosa, IVB distant
**FIGO 2023** endometrium adds histological type, LVSI and molecular class: POLE-mutated early disease downstaged (IAm-POLEmut), p53-abnormal with myometrial invasion upstaged (IICm-p53abn)
**Lynch syndrome** (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2): endometrial cancer is often the sentinel cancer in women; risk-reducing hysterectomy + BSO after childbearing
**RMI I** = U × M × CA-125; U = 0/1/3 (0, 1, ≥2 USG features: multilocular, solid, bilateral, ascites, metastases); M = 1 premenopausal, 3 postmenopausal; >200 → refer (RCOG)

**IOTA simple rules**: B-features (unilocular, solid <7 mm, acoustic shadows, smooth multilocular <10 cm, no flow) vs M-features (irregular solid, ascites, ≥4 papillary projections, irregular multilocular-solid ≥10 cm, very strong flow); only B = benign, only M = malignant, both/none = inconclusive
CA-125 false positives: endometriosis, PID, fibroids, pregnancy, menstruation, any peritoneal irritation – poor screening test in premenopausal women
Ovarian Ca: optimal cytoreduction = no gross residual (classic <1 cm); carboplatin + paclitaxel; PARP inhibitor (olaparib) maintenance in BRCA/HRD

traps.fix: Dysgerminoma – fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy + staging; very chemo/radiosensitive (BEP)

traps.trap: Ovarian serous carcinoma with endometrial metastasis
traps.fix: Oestrogen-secreting granulosa cell tumour (inhibin ↑) causing endometrial hyperplasia/carcinoma

traps.stem: Fibroma of ovary with ascites and right pleural effusion
traps.fix: Meigs syndrome – benign; effusions resolve after tumour removal

title: AUB (PALM-COEIN), fibroids, adenomyosis & endometriosis
subject: OBGY
anchor: Heavy menstrual bleeding + firm irregular enlarged uterus = leiomyoma; submucosal fibroid gives most bleeding & infertility
Multiparous 40s, dysmenorrhoea + menorrhagia, uniformly 'globular' tender uterus ≤12–14 wk = adenomyosis
Dysmenorrhoea + deep dyspareunia + dyschezia + infertility, nodular uterosacrals, fixed retroverted uterus = endometriosis
Fibroid + acute pain, fever, tenderness in mid-pregnancy = red degeneration → conservative

tables.title: Adenomyosis vs fibroid
head: Feature
Adenomyosis
Leiomyoma
rows: Irregular, asymmetric, can be very large
Ill-defined, no pseudocapsule – cannot be enucleated
Myometrial cysts, venetian-blind shadowing, junctional zone ≥12 mm on MRI
Well-defined hypoechoic mass, whorled, edge shadowing

points: **PALM-COEIN** (FIGO 2011, revised 2018): structural – Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy & hyperplasia; non-structural – Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not yet classified. 2018 revision moved anticoagulant-related AUB to AUB-C
Commonest cause of AUB in adolescents: anovulation (AUB-O); look for von Willebrand disease (commonest inherited coagulopathy)

HMB medical therapy: **LNG-IUS first line** (NICE) if no large fibroid/cavity distortion; tranexamic acid, mefenamic acid, COCs, progestins; acute severe bleeding – high-dose oestrogen or tranexamic acid
**Fibroid degenerations**: hyaline (commonest), cystic, calcific (postmenopausal, 'womb stone'), red/carneous (pregnancy, 2nd trimester), sarcomatous (rare, <1%)
Fibroids: GnRH agonist 3 months pre-op shrinks fibroid and corrects anaemia; ulipristal (SPRM) restricted for liver injury; oral GnRH antagonists (relugolix/elagolix) with add-back
Avoid myomectomy at caesarean (haemorrhage) except pedunculated fibroids
**Endometriosis**: Sampson retrograde menstruation (commonest theory); ovary commonest site (chocolate cyst/endometrioma – 'ground-glass' homogeneous echoes); powder-burn and red-flame lesions
**rASRM** stages: I minimal (1–5), II mild (6–15), III moderate (16–40), IV severe (>40); stage does not correlate with pain
Endometriosis diagnosis: laparoscopy + histology classic gold standard (ESHRE 2022 accepts imaging diagnosis); 1st-line medical: NSAIDs + COCs/progestins (dienogest); GnRH analogue with add-back
Endometriosis-associated ovarian cancers: clear cell and endometrioid

title: PCOS, amenorrhoea work-up, ovulation induction & OHSS
subject: OBGY
anchor: Oligomenorrhoea + hirsutism/acne + obesity + acanthosis nigricans = PCOS (Rotterdam 2 of 3, after excluding mimics)
Secondary amenorrhoea after D&C (or genital TB in India), no withdrawal bleed even with oestrogen + progestin = Asherman syndrome
Failure of lactation + amenorrhoea after massive PPH = Sheehan syndrome
Primary amenorrhoea, normal breasts, absent uterus: XX with normal pubic hair = MRKH; XY with scanty pubic hair = androgen insensitivity
algorithm:
Secondary amenorrhoea
→ Urine/serum β-hCG (pregnancy first, always)
→ TSH, prolactin (± FSH, LH, androgens)
→ Progestin challenge (MPA 10 mg × 5–10 days)
  → Withdrawal bleed → adequate oestrogen + patent outflow → anovulation (PCOS)
  → No bleed → oestrogen + progestin challenge (CEE 1.25 mg × 21 d + MPA last 5 d)
     → No bleed → outflow tract defect (Asherman) → hysteroscopy
     → Bleed → FSH/LH
        → High → ovarian failure (POI if <40 y; karyotype if <30 y)
        → Low/normal → hypothalamic–pituitary cause → MRI sella
PCOS anovulatory infertility → weight loss → letrozole 2.5–7.5 mg D3–7 (1st line) → clomiphene → gonadotropins or laparoscopic ovarian drilling → IVF

head: Feature
Turner (45,X)
MRKH (46,XX)
Complete AIS (46,XY)
rows: Short stature, webbed neck, coarctation, bicuspid AV, horseshoe kidney
Blind vaginal pouch, renal (unilateral agenesis) & skeletal anomalies

points: **Rotterdam 2003**: any 2 of oligo/anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovarian morphology – after excluding thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia, NCCAH (17-OH-progesterone), Cushing's, androgen-secreting tumour

PCOM (International PCOS guideline 2018/2023): ≥20 follicles (2–9 mm) per ovary and/or ovarian volume ≥10 mL; older criterion ≥12 follicles. 2023: AMH may replace USG in adults; USG not used <8 y after menarche
LH:FSH >2 is common but is NOT a diagnostic criterion; long-term risks: T2DM, endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, dyslipidaemia, OSA
**Letrozole** is first-line ovulation induction in PCOS (higher live-birth rate than clomiphene, PPCOS-II trial)
**Primary amenorrhoea**: no menses by 15 y with secondary sex characteristics, or by 13 y without breast development (older texts: 16 y). Commonest cause: gonadal dysgenesis (Turner), then MRKH
**Secondary amenorrhoea**: absent menses for 3 months (regular cycles) or 6 months (irregular). Commonest cause = pregnancy; then PCOS
**POI**: <40 y, amenorrhoea ≥4 months + FSH >25 IU/L on 2 occasions ≥4 wk apart (ESHRE)
**Asherman**: intrauterine adhesions after postpartum/post-abortal curettage; hysteroscopy diagnostic and therapeutic (adhesiolysis + oestrogen ± IUCD/balloon)
**Kallmann**: hypogonadotropic hypogonadism + anosmia (GnRH neuron migration defect, KAL1/ANOS1)

**OHSS**: iatrogenic, after hCG trigger (early) or with pregnancy hCG (late); VEGF-driven capillary leak → ascites, haemoconcentration, oliguria, thrombosis. Prevention: antagonist protocol + GnRH-agonist trigger, freeze-all, cabergoline. Risk: PCOS, young, high AMH/E₂

subject: OBGY
anchor: Deceleration that mirrors the contraction = early (head compression); starts after the peak = late (uteroplacental insufficiency); abrupt V/W-shaped, variable timing = variable (cord compression)
Turtle sign after delivery of head = shoulder dystocia → McRoberts + suprapubic pressure first
Rh-negative mother, Rh-positive baby → anti-D 300 µg within 72 h; Kleihauer–Betke if large FMH suspected
Lambda (twin-peak) sign = dichorionic; T sign = monochorionic

points: **WHO modified partograph** (2000): plotting starts in active phase at 4 cm; alert line 1 cm/h; action line 4 h to the right. **WHO 2018/Labour Care Guide 2020**: active phase starts at 5 cm and the fixed 1 cm/h alert line is dropped
**Bishop score**: dilatation, effacement, station (0–3 each), consistency, position (0–2 each), max 13; ≥8 favourable; ≤6 needs ripening (PGE₂ dinoprostone, misoprostol 25 µg PV, Foley catheter)
Reactive NST: ≥2 accelerations of ≥15 bpm for ≥15 s in 20 min (≥32 wk). Fetal scalp pH <7.20 → deliver

**Shoulder dystocia (HELPERR)**: Help, Evaluate episiotomy, Legs (McRoberts), suprapubic Pressure (Rubin I), Enter (Rubin II, Woods screw), Remove posterior arm, Roll to all-fours (Gaskin); last resort Zavanelli, symphysiotomy, cleidotomy. **No fundal pressure**. Commonest injury: Erb palsy (C5–C6)
Engaging diameters: flexed vertex suboccipitobregmatic 9.5 cm; face submentobregmatic 9.5 cm; brow mentovertical ~14 cm (undeliverable vaginally at term)
Breech is the commonest malpresentation; ECV from 36 wk (nullipara) / 37 wk (multipara); aftercoming head – Mauriceau–Smellie–Veit or Piper forceps; extended arms – Lovset
Face: mentum-anterior can deliver vaginally; persistent mentum-posterior → caesarean
**Anti-D**: 300 µg (1500 IU) IM covers ~30 mL fetal whole blood (15 mL RBC); routine at 28 wk + within 72 h of delivery of Rh+ baby; 50 µg for events <12 wk (ACOG). Useless once sensitised
Sensitised (ICT positive, critical titre ~1:16) → serial MCA-PSV Doppler; >1.5 MoM → cordocentesis + intrauterine (intravascular) transfusion
Chorionicity best determined at 11–14 wk; TTTS (MCDA) – Quintero staging, fetoscopic laser 16–26 wk

algorithm:
CTG: read in order — DR C BRAVADO (Define Risk, Contractions, Baseline RAte, Variability, Accels, Decels, Overall)
→ Baseline 110–160 bpm; <110 bradycardia (>10 min), >160 tachycardia
→ Variability 5–25 bpm = reassuring; <5 for >50 min (or sinusoidal) = non-reassuring
→ Accelerations ≥15 bpm for ≥15 s (≥10 × 10 s if <32 wk) = fetal well-being
→ Decelerations: what is their timing vs contraction?
  Early (mirror image, nadir with peak) → head compression, benign
  Variable (abrupt V/U/W shape, vary in timing) → cord compression → change position, amnioinfusion, check cord prolapse
  Late (start after the peak, nadir after) → uteroplacental insufficiency (hypoxia) → left lateral, stop oxytocin, O₂ , treat hypotension; if persistent → expedite delivery
  Prolonged (>2 min, <3 min) → look for cause; >3 min = bradycardia → emergency
→ Sinusoidal pattern → severe fetal anaemia (Rh isoimmunisation, fetomaternal haemorrhage) → emergency
Partogram (WHO): latent phase to 3–5 cm (not plotted); active phase plotted from ≥4 cm (WHO 2018 ≥5 cm)
  Alert line = 1 cm/h from 4 cm; action line 4 h to the right of it
  Crossing action line → reassess: augment (ARM, oxytocin) if hypotonic / CS if obstructed (CPD, malpresentation)

points: **GDM – DIPSI/GoI 2018**: 75 g oral glucose, non-fasting, 2-h value ≥140 mg/dL; test at first ANC visit and again at 24–28 wk
**IADPSG/WHO 2013** (75 g fasting OGTT, any one): fasting ≥92, 1 h ≥180, 2 h ≥153 mg/dL. Carpenter–Coustan (100 g, any two): 95/180/155/140

Overt diabetes in pregnancy: fasting ≥126 mg/dL, HbA1c ≥6.5% or random ≥200 mg/dL. GDM targets: fasting <95, 1 h <140, 2 h <120 mg/dL; MNT first, insulin if targets unmet in ~2 wk; postpartum OGTT at 6–12 wk
Pregestational DM: commonest anomaly cardiac (VSD, TGA); most specific – caudal regression syndrome

**Anaemia in pregnancy (WHO)**: Hb <11 g/dL; mild 10–10.9, moderate 7–9.9, severe <7 g/dL. Anemia Mukt Bharat: 60 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid daily from 2nd trimester for 180 days, continued 180 days postpartum
**Physiology**: plasma volume ↑ ~40–50% vs RBC mass ↑ ~20–30% → haemodilution; cardiac output ↑ 30–50% (highest immediately after delivery); SVR and BP fall mid-pregnancy
Respiratory: tidal volume and minute ventilation ↑, FRC ↓ ~20%, RR and vital capacity unchanged → compensated respiratory alkalosis (PaCO₂ ~30 mmHg)
Renal: GFR ↑ ~50% → creatinine, urea and uric acid fall; physiological glycosuria; right > left hydroureter
Coagulation: fibrinogen and factors VII, VIII, X ↑ (hypercoagulable); ALP ↑ (placental); TBG ↑ → total T4 ↑, free T4 normal

title: Neonatal resuscitation (NRP): golden minute to adrenaline
subject: Pediatrics
anchor: Ventilation is the single most important step in neonatal resuscitation
Apnoea/gasping or HR <100 after initial steps → PPV within the golden minute
HR <60 despite 30 s of PPV that moves the chest → intubate, compressions 3:1 with 100% O₂
Rising heart rate = most sensitive indicator of effective resuscitation
algorithm:
Birth → 3 questions: term? good tone? breathing/crying?
  → All yes → stay with mother: warm, dry, skin-to-skin, delayed cord clamping (≥30–60 s)
  → Any no → initial steps under radiant warmer: warm, position (sniffing), clear airway only if needed, dry, stimulate
→ Apnoea/gasping or HR <100 → PPV 40–60/min (21% O₂ if ≥35 wk; 21–30% if <35 wk) + SpO₂ probe on right hand ± ECG
  → Laboured breathing / persistent cyanosis only → position, clear airway, SpO₂, O₂ as needed, consider CPAP
→ Check chest rise; if no rise → MR SOPA corrective steps
→ HR <100 after 30 s effective PPV → continue PPV, consider alternative airway
→ HR <60 → intubate/LMA, chest compressions 3:1 (90 compressions + 30 breaths/min), FiO₂ 100%, ECG, UVC
→ HR still <60 after 60 s of compressions → adrenaline 0.02 mg/kg IV (range 0.01–0.03) of 0.1 mg/mL, repeat q3–5 min; ETT 0.1 mg/kg (0.05–0.1) while access obtained
→ Suspected hypovolaemia → NS 10 mL/kg over 5–10 min
→ No detectable HR after ~20 min of full resuscitation → discuss stopping
points: **Golden minute**: initial steps + reassessment + start of PPV within 60 s of birth
**MR SOPA**: Mask adjust, Reposition head, Suction mouth then nose, Open mouth, Pressure increase, Alternative airway (ETT or laryngeal mask)
PPV pressures: ~20–25 cmH₂O (higher for first breaths in some term babies), PEEP ~5 cmH₂O; rate 40–60/min ('breathe-two-three')
Compressions: two-thumb encircling technique, lower third of sternum, depth one-third of AP chest diameter; 3:1 ratio = 120 events/min
**Meconium-stained, non-vigorous** baby: no routine intubation for tracheal suction (since 2015) – do initial steps and start PPV
Preterm <32 wk: polyethylene wrap/bag without drying + radiant warmer; target temperature 36.5–37.5 °C
ETT size: <28 wk 2.5 mm; 28–34 wk 3.0 mm; >34 wk 3.5 mm; depth (cm at lip) ≈ weight in kg + 6 (or nasal–tragus length + 1)
**APGAR** at 1 and 5 min (every 5 min till 20 min if <7 at 5 min); it is NOT used to decide when to start resuscitation
Laryngeal mask is an alternative airway for ≥34 wk / ≥2 kg babies when mask ventilation or intubation fails

points: **Silverman–Anderson** score (preterm): upper chest retraction, lower chest retraction, xiphoid retraction, nasal flaring, expiratory grunt; 0–10, higher = worse (≥7 impending failure)
**Downes** score (term): RR, cyanosis, air entry, grunting, retractions; 0–10, >6 impending respiratory failure
Lung maturity: L/S ratio ≥2 and presence of phosphatidylglycerol; antenatal steroids betamethasone 12 mg IM × 2 doses 24 h apart (or dexamethasone 6 mg × 4, 12-hourly) for 24–34 wk
Surfactant (poractant 200 mg/kg, beractant 100 mg/kg) via INSURE or LISA when FiO₂ >0.30–0.40 on CPAP
**Kramer zones**: 1 head/neck ~5, 2 upper trunk ~10, 3 lower trunk/thighs ~12, 4 arms/legs ~15, 5 palms/soles >15 mg/dL (cephalocaudal spread)
**Bhutani nomogram**: hour-specific TSB for ≥35 wk; high-risk zone >95th percentile, high-intermediate 76–95th, low-intermediate 40–75th, low <40th
**Phototherapy**: blue light 460–490 nm; main mechanism structural isomerisation to lumirubin (excreted without conjugation); bronze baby syndrome if conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia
**Exchange transfusion**: double volume (~160–170 mL/kg) removes ~85% of RBCs and ~50% of bilirubin; urgently if signs of acute bilirubin encephalopathy

**Kernicterus**: unconjugated bilirubin stains basal ganglia (globus pallidus), subthalamic nucleus, hippocampus, cranial-nerve nuclei; chronic tetrad – choreoathetosis, sensorineural hearing loss, upward gaze palsy, dental enamel dysplasia
Breastfeeding jaundice (1st week, inadequate intake) vs breast-milk jaundice (late, 2nd–3rd week, continue breastfeeding). Pale stools + conjugated jaundice → biliary atresia (Kasai before ~60 days)

title: Congenital heart disease, Eisenmenger, PDA & Kawasaki
subject: Pediatrics
anchor: Cyanotic child who squats after play, ejection systolic murmur, single S2, boot-shaped heart with oligaemic lungs = ToF
Cyanosis from day 1 without murmur, egg-on-side heart, plethoric lungs = TGA → PGE1, balloon atrial septostomy, arterial switch
Radio-femoral delay, upper-limb hypertension, rib notching, '3' sign = coarctation of aorta
Fever ≥5 days + conjunctival injection, strawberry tongue, extremity oedema/desquamation, rash, cervical node = Kawasaki → IVIG + aspirin
algorithm:
Tet (hypercyanotic) spell
→ Knee-chest position (↑ SVR) + calm the child
→ O₂
→ Morphine 0.1–0.2 mg/kg SC/IM/IV (abolishes hyperpnoea, relaxes infundibulum)
→ IV fluids; sodium bicarbonate for acidosis
→ Persistent: phenylephrine (↑ SVR) or IV propranolol/esmolol; ketamine
→ Avoid inotropes/digoxin (worsen infundibular spasm)
→ After spell: oral propranolol, correct iron deficiency; plan BT shunt or total correction
Duct-dependent neonate (cyanotic or shocked) → start PGE1 (alprostadil) before definitive diagnosis; watch for apnoea

tables.title: Cyanotic CHD – radiographic signs
head: Lesion
Sign
Discriminators
rows: Boot-shaped heart (coeur en sabot), concave pulmonary bay, oligaemic lungs; right arch ~25%
VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, RVH; no CHF; severity depends on RVOTO; RAD
Egg on side / egg on a string (narrow mediastinum), plethoric lungs
Commonest cyanotic CHD presenting in newborn; IDM; needs mixing (ASD/PDA/VSD)
Obstructed (infracardiac) type: small heart + pulmonary venous congestion – surgical emergency
Apical displacement of septal/posterior tricuspid leaflets; maternal lithium; WPW
Left axis deviation with cyanosis (LV dominant)

tables.title: Kawasaki disease – diagnosis and treatment
head: Item
Detail
rows: Fever ≥5 days + ≥4 of 5: bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis (limbal sparing); lips/oral changes (strawberry tongue, cracked lips); polymorphous rash; extremity changes (oedema/erythema → periungual desquamation wk 2–3); cervical node ≥1.5 cm (usually unilateral)
↑ ESR/CRP, sterile pyuria, ↓ albumin; thrombocytosis in 2nd week
IVIG 2 g/kg single infusion (ideally within 10 days) + aspirin moderate/high dose, then low dose 3–5 mg/kg/day for 6–8 wk
Coronary artery aneurysm (echo at diagnosis, 1–2 wk, 4–6 wk); commonest cause of acquired heart disease in children in developed countries

points: **VSD** = commonest CHD overall; **ASD secundum** = commonest ASD (wide fixed split S2); **ToF** = commonest cyanotic CHD overall (after infancy); **TGA** = commonest cyanotic CHD in the newborn

**ToF complications**: cerebral thrombosis (<2 y, polycythaemia/relative iron deficiency), brain abscess (>2 y), infective endocarditis; murmur is from RVOT stenosis (not VSD) – it shortens during a spell
**TGA**: PGE1 to keep duct open → balloon atrial septostomy (Rashkind) → arterial switch (Jatene) within first 2–3 weeks

**Coarctation**: rib notching on inferior margins of 3rd–8th ribs (intercostal collaterals; usually after 5 y); '3' sign on CXR, reversed 3 ('E') on barium swallow; associated bicuspid aortic valve, Turner syndrome

**Eisenmenger**: long-standing L→R shunt → pulmonary vascular disease → reversal (R→L); loud single P2, murmur softens, cyanosis/clubbing; surgery contraindicated (heart–lung transplant); pregnancy contraindicated
PDA with Eisenmenger → **differential cyanosis** (toes cyanosed/clubbed, fingers pink)

**PDA**: continuous machinery murmur, wide pulse pressure; congenital rubella, prematurity. Close with ibuprofen (preferred), indomethacin or paracetamol; keep open with PGE1 (alprostadil) in duct-dependent lesions (TGA, pulmonary atresia, HLHS, critical coarctation)
Indomethacin side effects: renal failure, NEC, GI bleed, platelet dysfunction

Down syndrome: AVSD (endocardial cushion defect) is the characteristic lesion; Turner: bicuspid AV > coarctation; Noonan: pulmonary stenosis; Williams: supravalvular AS; DiGeorge: truncus / interrupted arch

traps.stem: Child with ToF in a tet spell; resident starts digoxin for 'heart failure'
traps.fix: Inotropes worsen infundibular spasm; ToF does not cause CHF – knee-chest, O₂, morphine, fluids, phenylephrine, β-blocker

traps.stem: Neonate with TGA, SpO₂ 60%, on PGE1. Next step?
traps.trap: Immediate total correction without stabilisation, or indomethacin
traps.fix: Balloon atrial septostomy if mixing inadequate, then arterial switch; never close the duct

traps.stem: Adolescent with VSD now cyanosed, murmur has disappeared, loud P2
traps.fix: Eisenmenger syndrome – shunt reversal; closure now contraindicated

title: Inborn errors of metabolism & chromosomal syndromes
subject: Pediatrics
anchor: Well at birth, deteriorates after milk feeds with vomiting, jaundice, hepatomegaly, E. coli sepsis, oil-drop cataract = galactosemia
Fair-skinned child with musty/mousy odour, eczema, intellectual disability = PKU
Neonatal encephalopathy + sweet maple-syrup urine + fencing/bicycling movements = MSUD
Encephalopathic neonate with high ammonia and respiratory alkalosis (no acidosis) = urea cycle defect

head: Syndrome
Karyotype
Hallmarks
Heart / other
rows: Trisomy 21 (95% non-disjunction, mostly maternal meiosis I; ~4% Robertsonian 14;21)
Flat facies, upslanting fissures, epicanthus, Brushfield spots, single palmar crease, sandal gap, hypotonia
AVSD; duodenal atresia, Hirschsprung, ALL/AML-M7, hypothyroidism, early Alzheimer, atlanto-axial instability
Clenched hands with overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom feet, prominent occiput, micrognathia
VSD; quad screen: all markers low
Holoprosencephaly, cleft lip/palate, microphthalmia, postaxial polydactyly, scalp defects (aplasia cutis)
Lymphoedema of hands/feet at birth, webbed neck, short stature, shield chest, cubitus valgus, short 4th metacarpal, streak gonads
Bicuspid AV, coarctation; horseshoe kidney; normal IQ
Tall, eunuchoid, gynaecomastia, small firm testes, azoospermia
↑ FSH/LH, ↓ testosterone; ↑ breast cancer; commonest cause of male hypogonadism

points: **PKU**: phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency (AR); tyrosine becomes essential; ↓ melanin; Guthrie (bacterial inhibition) test → now tandem MS, after 24–48 h of feeds; Phe-restricted diet for life; BH4-deficiency variant ('malignant PKU') needs BH4 + neurotransmitter precursors
**Maternal PKU** (uncontrolled) → microcephaly, intellectual disability, CHD in non-PKU fetus – restrict Phe before conception
**MSUD**: branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase (thiamine-dependent) → leucine, isoleucine, valine; cerebral oedema; DNPH test positive; acute – dialysis, BCAA-free feeds, trial of thiamine

**Galactosemia** (GALT): urine reducing substance positive (Benedict) but glucose-oxidase strip negative; stop lactose (soy formula); long-term POI and speech problems despite diet. Galactokinase deficiency: cataract only
**Urea cycle crisis**: stop protein, IV glucose (10%), sodium benzoate/phenylbutyrate, arginine; haemodialysis for very high ammonia

**Homocystinuria vs Marfan**: lens dislocation downward/inferonasal vs upward/superotemporal; intellectual disability + thrombosis (arterial & venous) vs normal IQ + aortic root dilatation/dissection; AR (cystathionine β-synthase) vs AD (FBN1). Homocystinuria: pyridoxine (~50% respond), betaine, low-methionine diet; nitroprusside test

**Fragile X**: CGG repeat >200 in FMR1 (Xq27.3) → methylation/silencing; commonest inherited cause of intellectual disability (Down = commonest genetic cause); long face, large ears, prominent jaw, macro-orchidism, autism, MVP. Premutation (55–200) → FXTAS, POI. Diagnosis: PCR + Southern blot
Down first-trimester screen: ↑ free β-hCG, ↓ PAPP-A, ↑ NT. Quadruple test: ↓ AFP, ↑ hCG, ↓ uE3, ↑ inhibin A. Trisomy 18: AFP, hCG, uE3 all low

traps.fix: Urea cycle defect – respiratory alkalosis without ketoacidosis; organic acidaemias have high-AG metabolic acidosis + ketosis

traps.fix: Homocystinuria – downward lens dislocation, thrombosis and intellectual disability; Marfan lens goes up and out

traps.fix: Dipstick detects only glucose; Benedict test (reducing substance) will be positive – confirm GALT enzyme assay, stop lactose immediately

title: Childhood exanthems & India UIP schedule
subject: Pediatrics
anchor: High fever + cough, coryza, conjunctivitis + Koplik spots → rash from behind ears spreading downward on day 4 = measles
Infant with 3–5 days of high fever, rash appears as fever settles = roseola (HHV-6)
Slapped-cheek face then lacy rash on limbs = erythema infectiosum (parvovirus B19) – aplastic crisis in haemolytic anaemia, hydrops in pregnancy
Sandpaper rash, Pastia lines, circumoral pallor, strawberry tongue after sore throat = scarlet fever (GAS)

Agent
Discriminating features
Key complication

Otitis media (commonest), pneumonia (commonest cause of death), diarrhoea, encephalitis, SSPE years later

tables.title: India UIP (current)
head: Age
Vaccines
rows: BCG (till 1 y), OPV-0 (within 15 days), Hepatitis B birth dose (within 24 h)
MR-1, JE-1 (endemic districts), PCV booster, fIPV-3 (added 2023), Vitamin A 1 lakh IU
MR-2, JE-2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster, Vitamin A 2 lakh IU (then 6-monthly till 5 y)
Td-1 early in pregnancy, Td-2 4 weeks later (Td booster if vaccinated within 3 y)

points: Measles: **vitamin A** 2 doses on consecutive days (<6 mo 50,000 IU; 6–11 mo 1 lakh IU; ≥12 mo 2 lakh IU), 3rd dose at 2–4 wk if eye signs; measles is infectious 4 days before to 4 days after rash
fIPV = 0.1 mL intradermal fractional dose; pentavalent = DPT + Hep B + Hib
**True contraindications**: anaphylaxis to a previous dose/component; encephalopathy within 7 days of a pertussis-containing dose → further pertussis contraindicated (give DT/Td)

Live vaccines (BCG, OPV, MR/MMR, rotavirus, varicella, live JE) are avoided in pregnancy and severe immunodeficiency; rotavirus also contraindicated with history of intussusception or SCID; symptomatic HIV – no BCG

**Not contraindications**: minor illness/low-grade fever, diarrhoea, malnutrition, prematurity (vaccinate at chronological age), ongoing antibiotics, breastfeeding, family history of seizures, egg allergy for MMR
Two live parenteral vaccines: same day or ≥4 weeks apart; after immunoglobulin/blood products defer measles-containing vaccine (3–11 months depending on product)
Varicella: exposed newborn of a mother whose rash appeared 5 days before to 2 days after delivery → VZIG (severe neonatal varicella)
Congenital varicella (maternal infection 8–20 wk): cicatricial skin scars, limb hypoplasia, eye and CNS defects

title: SAM, WHO 10 steps, malnutrition grading, vitamin A & rickets
subject: Pediatrics
anchor: 6–59 mo with WHZ <−3 SD or MUAC <11.5 cm or bilateral pitting oedema = SAM
Oedema, flaky-paint dermatosis, flag sign, fatty liver, apathy = kwashiorkor; severe wasting, 'old-man' face, alert & hungry = marasmus
Craniotabes, rachitic rosary, widened wrists, Harrison sulcus, bow legs; cupping & fraying of metaphysis = rickets
SAM: no iron in stabilisation phase; F-75 first, then F-100/RUTF
algorithm:
SAM child → appetite test + look for complications (hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, shock, infection, poor appetite, severe oedema)
→ Uncomplicated + passes appetite test → community management with RUTF + oral amoxicillin
→ Complicated → inpatient WHO 10 steps
  Stabilisation (days 1–7): steps 1–7 – treat/prevent hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dehydration (ReSoMal), electrolytes (K, Mg), infection (antibiotics to all), micronutrients (no iron), cautious feeding with F-75
  Rehabilitation (wk 2–6): catch-up growth with F-100/RUTF, start iron, sensory stimulation, prepare for follow-up
→ Discharge: WHZ ≥ −2 or MUAC ≥12.5 cm (same indicator as at admission) with no oedema for ≥2 wk

tables.title: Malnutrition classifications
head: System
Indicator
Grades
rows: SAM: WHZ <−3 SD / MUAC <11.5 cm / bilateral oedema. MAM: WHZ −3 to −2 / MUAC 11.5–12.5 cm
60–80% + oedema = kwashiorkor; 60–80% no oedema = undernutrition; <60% + oedema = marasmic kwashiorkor; <60% no oedema = marasmus

points: **F-75**: 75 kcal + 0.9 g protein/100 mL, given 130 mL/kg/day (100 mL/kg/day if severe oedema) 2–3 hourly. **F-100**: 100 kcal + 2.9 g protein/100 mL; target 150–220 kcal/kg/day in rehabilitation
Hypoglycaemia in SAM: blood glucose <54 mg/dL (3 mmol/L) → 50 mL 10% glucose orally/NG or 5 mL/kg 10% dextrose IV
**ReSoMal**: low sodium, high potassium ORS for SAM; avoid IV fluids unless in shock (risk of heart failure)
Good weight gain in rehabilitation: >10 g/kg/day; watch for **refeeding syndrome** (hypophosphataemia)
**Vitamin A prophylaxis (India)**: 1 lakh IU at 9 mo with MR-1, then 2 lakh IU every 6 months till 5 y – 9 doses in all. Treatment of xerophthalmia: age-specific dose on day 0, day 1 and day 14
Xerophthalmia (WHO): XN night blindness (earliest symptom), X1A conjunctival xerosis, X1B Bitot spots, X2 corneal xerosis, X3A ulcer <1/3, X3B keratomalacia ≥1/3, XS scar, XF fundus
Rickets: earliest clinical sign craniotabes (3–6 mo; ping-pong skull); earliest radiological sign loss of zone of provisional calcification; best X-ray: wrist (ulna) and knee
Nutritional rickets treatment: vitamin D 2000 IU/day × 3 months (global consensus 2016) or stoss therapy 6 lakh IU single oral dose (Indian practice), plus calcium; healing line visible in 3–4 weeks

traps.fix: No iron in stabilisation phase (worsens infection/free radicals); start iron in rehabilitation phase (~week 2)

traps.fix: Oral/NG ReSoMal 5 mL/kg every 30 min for 2 h, then 5–10 mL/kg/h; IV only for shock (cautious 15 mL/kg)

traps.fix: X-linked hypophosphataemic rickets (↑ FGF23) – oral phosphate + calcitriol (or burosumab)
